newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PRESSURE MOUNTS FOR HODGSON AT INTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PRESSURE MOUNTS FOR HODGSON AT INTER.

text.p: Italian club Internazionale have yet to lose a game this season but that has not silenced media criticism of their English coach Roy Hodgson.
Inter are currently third in the league, two points behind leaders Juventus and one point behind city rivals AC Milan, while they are still on course in both the UEFA and Italian Cups.
Although Inter have picked up points and results, their overall play has been far from impressive and in particular has disappointed club owner, petrol industrialist Massimo Moratti.

Last week Inter took a 3-0 lead into the second leg of their UEFA Cup tie against modest French side Guingamp and appeared to take things easy in a 1-1 home draw at the San Siro, prompting Moratti's anger.
"I'm most disappointed. This is not the way to do things. These gentlemen (Inter players) ought to show more respect both for the fans and the game itself."
Then Following Sunday's 1-1 away draw with Atalanta, Moratti again expressed his disappointment after a match in which Atalanta equalised in the 86th minute.
"This was a game that we ought not to have thrown away".

Media speculation suggests that Moratti believes Hodgson should take a tougher line with his players, with Milan sports daily "Gazzetta Dello Sport" commenting: "It's up to Hodgson to sort things out...the club expects him to be a bit more of a seargant major with the players"

Such media comment is not new. Even before the season began, "Gazzetta Dello Sport" had written: "A problem does exist and Hodgson is the problem. Will he prove capable of leading the potentially great side created for him by President Moratti ?"
Hodgson, however, is defended by his aide, the former Inter and Italy defender Giacinto Facchetti.
"This year we've made a lot of changes and of all the big names, we're the one with most room for improvement...but you need time".

Inter signed Dutch midfielder Aron Winter, Frenchmen Youri Djorkaeff and Jocelyn Angloma, Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano and Swiss midfielder Ciriaco Sforza this summer joining a squad which already contained Englishman Paul Ince and Argentine Javier Zanetti.
Speaking before the season, Hodgson acknowledged that his biggest difficulty would be to blend so many different talents, adding:
"The job of coaching, being a good a coach, is to take a bunch of individuals and make them into a team. That's my task"

Although media speculation argues that Hodgson is not in danger of imminent dismissal, reports still go on to suggest the names of current Italian coach Arrigo Sacchi, current Argentine coach Daniel Passarella and current Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello as possible future successors on the Inter bench.
